current.text: CJ McCollum is in Atlanta and is projected to start with Nickeil Alexander-Walker, Dyson Daniels, Johnson and Onyeka Okongwu. Each starter should play 30 or more minutes. The team has no true point guard, so McCollum, Alexander-Walker, Johnson and Daniels share the ball handling.

Last season Johnson played about two-thirds of the games without Trae Young or McCollum. When McCollum played, Johnson's assists fell by about one per game. His time on the ball, steals, blocks and shooting efficiency also dropped, and he was not a top 30 player in that stretch.
2025-26 was his first healthy season and came with a big jump in minutes. His shooting dropped in the second half and in the playoffs, and his defensive stats faded late in the season.
Experts expect sharing creation with McCollum to cut his assists, usage, steals and FG% a bit. They think repeating last season's numbers will be hard.
Most experts say he is not a first-round player in 9-cat and is overdrafted at picks 9 to 12. One speaker said pick 10 is slightly early but will not sink a team.
In category leagues experts put his fair value in round two, around picks 15 to 20. He should not fall past pick 20.
He went for 33 USD in an expert auction mock draft.

With a March 28 season end, Atlanta plays 4, 4 and 3 games in the fantasy playoff weeks. The team has 14 back-to-backs, but resting players is not a concern, and the team did not shut players down last season.

durable.text: He is excellent in points, rebounds and assists. His rebounds and assists are league outliers, and his playmaking is rare for a forward: about eight assists per game.
He commits many turnovers. TO is his clear weak category.
Experts call his percentages and his three-point shooting iffy. Projections put his FG% and FT% near the pool average.
He was injured in every season before 2025-26. The injuries included wrist and shoulder problems.
Experts disagree on his injury risk. Lloyd calls the past injuries fluky and is not concerned. Others call his medical history checkered and say the new narrative that he is reliable is ridiculous.
He is worth more in points leagues, where experts rate him a fine pick at 8 to 12, than in 9-cat. Points-based ranks overrate him for us.

note: Yahoo (46 USD value, 50 USD cost) and ESPN (56 USD value, 54.5 USD cost) price him as a first-rounder. Experts see him as a round-two player in 9-cat, closer to our league's 34 USD last season and the 33 USD mock result. He fits punt TO builds and teams that want rebounds and assists from a forward, so bid up to about 35 to 40 USD and let others pay first-round money. Early in the season, check his assists, FG% and steals next to McCollum, because experts expect those numbers to fall from last season's 7.9 assists and 48.9% FG.
